input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the uploaded text only on "\n" (`const lines = text.split("\n");`). Files exported from Windows tools use CRLF line endings, so each line (including the header) retains a trailing "\r". This shifts/corrupts the last column and makes the row length comparison fail, triggering "errors.rowShape" on row 1 for otherwise valid files. The parser needs to normalize/strip "\r" (e.g. split on /\r?\n/ or strip \r before splitting fields) to handle CRLF input.

text: This is clearly a CRLF line-ending issue: splitting only on "\n" leaves a trailing "\r" on the header/fields, causing the column count mismatch for Windows-exported files.
